_comment: Ids from owed-baseline.txt that the CURRENT golden no longer owes (moved to SKIP/FAIL, or
dropped from cells.json) — named here with an owner and a rationale so the loss is a decision,
not silence. replay.sh reads this file; an id it does not cover is RED. `cells` is a regex over
the cell id (same convention as accepted-differences.json's `cells` field).
Coverage GROWING (a new id owed that was not in the baseline) needs no entry here — it is
always allowed and just printed; only a SHRINK needs to be named.
Nothing has been dropped from the 1.5.5 golden since owed-baseline.txt was generated from
golden/1.5.5/ledger.tsv's PASS rows. The entries below are of two shapes. A cell that has
never been owed is named so the reason it is not recorded is written down and owned, and so
the entry is already in place the day the cell is baselined and then re-loses its fixture. A
cell that IS owed but that THIS RECORDING HOST cannot produce is named so a host-shaped
absence can never be read as a pass; such an entry names what the host lacks, and expires
on a host that has it rather than being a decision to stop owing the cell.

accepted.rationale: needs a tool-use verb in the pinned mock; product decision on the six-dialect tool-use response shape. The cell declared a mock_control the mock resolves to no verb, and an unresolvable control is served as a healthy 200 — so the cell would have recorded the tool-less happy path while claiming to pin usageMetadata.toolUsePromptTokenCount. The control is removed and the cell stays needs_fixture (SKIP) until the mock can answer with the tool-use token term and the product decides what that answer looks like in each of the six dialects; inventing either here would put the oracle's own guess into the golden.

NO CONTAINER RUNTIME ON THE RECORDING HOST. The golden records PASS for all four plugins.store-persist cells, so these three are genuinely owed; a recording host that cannot stand the servers up reports them missing.candidate, and that loss is named here rather than passing in silence. testing/fleet-fixtures/store-services.sh is the ONLY provisioner for postgres/mysql/valkey and it is written on `docker run -d --rm` plus a `docker exec` readiness probe (its own header states why there is deliberately no compose file); measured on the recording host: no docker, and no podman/colima/lima/nerdctl, and no native postgres/mysqld/valkey-server/redis-server. plugins.store-persist|store-sqlite needs no server, DOES run here, and is deliberately NOT covered by this entry -- it is the load-bearing cell for the store kind's ABI-2 wire on a host like this one. SCOPE AND STANDING: this is the only family that would catch an ABI-2 regression on the three server-backed stores, so a green local run of the store-kind face line (gate/STORE-design-face-completion.md, the ABI-2/4 <-> 5 translator commit) must NOT be read as proving those three backends; the entry exists so that reading is impossible to make by accident. It expires the day the cells are recorded on a host with a container runtime -- a fleet box or CI, where the shadow-oracle job already stands the three services up -- and it is not a decision to stop owing them.
